subtopics.name: Reasons why Business Objectives may Change

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *TUI* is a holiday business that has over 100 years of experience. It offers customers a variety of holidays including staying in hotels, and river and ocean-going cruises. There are many extras that it offers to holiday makers including: car hire, extensions to the holiday and arranging day trips at all its holiday destinations. 
> 
> The business is well known and flies its customers to over 180 destinations around the world, including Greece, Turkey and Spain. It has 1,600 travel agencies and 27 million customers. Holidays can be booked by visiting a travel agency or online. 
> 
> *TUI *has holidays to meet the needs of all its customers: families, children, couples and those with disabilities.

Which **one** of the following is a non-financial objective?

Select **one** answer
parts.solution_md:
**The correct answer is B**

Personal satisfaction is a non-financial objective as it relates to personal fulfilment rather than money.

**A** is incorrect as generating wealth is a financial objective

**C** is incorrect as maximising profit is a financial objective

**D** is incorrect as regular income is a financial objective

parts.problem_md: Define the term **stakeholder**
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Anyone with an interest in / who is affected by a business **[1 mark]**
> 
> Award 1 mark for a correct definition of **stakeholder**.
> 
> Alternative acceptable answer:
> 
> - Any person or organisation that is influenced by or can influence the decisions of a business

> **[exam-tip]**
> When defining "stakeholder", make sure your answer captures two key ideas: that the person or group has an interest in the business, and that they are affected by (or can affect) its activities. A common mistake is to simply say "someone involved in a business" — this is too vague and may not earn the mark. Try to be specific about the relationship between the stakeholder and the business.

**[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *IKEA* is a well-known home furniture retailer with stores throughout the world. It was started in 1943 by Ingvar Kamprad when he was given some money by his father for doing well at school. He wanted to produce furniture at a price that people could afford to buy.
> 
> He realised that transporting furniture to customers was difficult as goods were often damaged. He developed flat packs to avoid damage. A flat pack contained all the materials needed to self-assemble a table, a chair or a bed.
> 
> All *IKEA* stores are run as franchises.

Which **one** of the following is a financial business objective?

Select **one** answer.
parts.solution_md:
**The correct answer is C** — Survival

Survival is a financial business objective as it relates to a business ensuring it generates enough revenue to cover its costs and continue operating.

**A** is incorrect as challenge is a non-financial objective

**B** is incorrect as social objectives is a non-financial objective

**D** is incorrect as personal satisfaction is a non-financial objective

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> One of *IKEA’s *aims is to keep up to date with the changes taking place in product design and meeting customers’ needs. To do this it has to introduce new and different products on a regular basis.

State **one** financial objective* IKEA* might have.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for a financial objective in the context of IKEA
> 
> - To increase revenue by regularly introducing new products that meet customer demand **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - IKEA wants to increase its market share in the sale of furniture **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - IKEA wants to survive in the competitive market of selling home goods **[1 mark]**
> 
> Accept any other appropriate response in the context of IKEA
> 
> Marks are not awarded for a financial objective that is not in the context of IKEA

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure your answer is a specifically *financial* objective — e.g. increasing revenue, profit or market share — rather than a non-financial objective such as improving customer satisfaction. Also, always link your answer to the context of the business in the extract. Simply writing "to make a profit" without any reference to IKEA or its products is unlikely to earn the mark.

**[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *Kraft Heinz* has different functional areas within the business. These functional areas work together to ensure that Kraft Heinz maintains high standards of production with limited waste material.
> 
> *Kraft Heinz *aims to be involved in the local area through various methods such as charity and sporting events.

State **one** financial objective* Kraft Heinz* might have.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for a financial objective Kraft Heinz might have in the context of the business
> 
> - To reduce waste in food production in order to lower costs **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - To increase its profit by increasing the number of different sauces they sell **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - To increase its market share by introducing new products such as Cool Whip to New Zealand **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - Accept any other appropriate response **[1 mark]**
> 
> Marks are not awarded for a financial objective that is not in the context of Kraft Heinz

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure your answer is a *financial* objective — this means it must relate to money, costs, revenue, profit or market share. A non-financial objective (e.g. "to improve customer satisfaction") would not be awarded the mark. Also, always link your answer to the context of Kraft Heinz rather than giving a generic response. Using details from the extract, such as reducing waste or being involved in the local area, will help demonstrate that your answer is applied to the business.

**[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *The Better Toy Store (TBTS*) is a children’s toy shop. *TBTS* has three shops in Singapore. Two of the shops are located in busy shopping malls and the third is located at the Jewel Changi Airport.
> 
> *TBTS* has a website for customers looking to buy toys online. *TBTS *selects toys to sell that are excellent for play, value, design and quality. All *TBTS* toys are environmentally friendly.

Which **one** of the following is a financial aim for a business?

Select **one** answer.
parts.solution_md:
**The correct answer is A** - Survival.

Survival is a financial aim because it relates to a business generating enough revenue to cover its costs and continue operating.

**B** is incorrect as challenge is a non-financial aim

**C** is incorrect as social objectives is a non-financial aim

**D** is incorrect as personal satisfaction is a non-financial aim

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> The *LEGO *Group is a privately-owned business in Denmark. The business was founded in 1932 by the Kristiansen family. The family still owns it. The name *LEGO *is an abbreviation of two Danish words, ‘leg godt’ which means ‘play well’. It is now one of the world’s largest manufacturers of toys with 15 factories and over 18,000 employees around the world.
> 
> *LEGO *manufactures toys, games and art materials for boys and girls of all ages, and products from films such as Star Wars and Harry Potter. It believes that children are the role models of the future and playing with *LEGO *can support children in a developing and complex world.
> 
> All 18,000 *LEGO *employees are full-time

State **one** financial objective for* LEGO*
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for a financial objective in the context of the business
> 
> - To increase sales revenue by expanding its product range into popular film brands such as Star Wars and Harry Potter **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - LEGO wants to maintain its market share in the toy sector **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - By achieving financial security, it allows LEGO to provide employment for its 18,000 employees **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - Accept any other appropriate response
> 
> Marks are not awarded for a financial objective that is not in the context of LEGO

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure your answer is a specifically *financial* objective — this means it should relate to money, revenue, profit, costs or financial stability. A common mistake is to give a non-financial objective such as "to improve brand awareness" or "to make better products". Also, always link your answer to the context of the business in the extract. For example, referencing LEGO's products, employees or market position will demonstrate application and help you secure the mark.

**[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *Huawei* is a leading global provider of information and communications technology, infrastructure and smart devices. In March 2011, over one million of its C8500 smartphones were sold in China following its launch.
> 
> It now manufactures a wide variety of different products including Huawei smartphones, watches and tablets. In recent years *Huawei* has won many awards. In 2018 it was named the 68th most valuable brand by Best Global Brands. In 2019 it introduced a smartphone which had new photographic technology.

Which **one **of the following is a financial objective?

Select **one** answer
parts.solution_md:
**The correct answer is B** – Market share

Market share is a financial objective as it relates to the proportion of total sales in a market achieved by a business.

**A** is incorrect as personal satisfaction is not a financial objective

**C** is incorrect as independence is not a financial objective

**D** is incorrect as control is not a financial objective

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> One of *TADS'* objectives is to expand by giving lessons for different musical instruments. To do this it will need to analyse its financial position.

Outline **one** possible financial objective, other than revenue, that TADS might have.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying a possible financial objective TADS might have and 1 further mark for outlining it in the context of the business
> 
> "Outline" requires identification of a relevant point plus a brief development or contextual link
> 
> - TADS could aim to increase its profit margins **[1 mark]**
> - This would help Ollie build up enough finance to invest in expanding the business into lessons for other musical instruments **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - TADS could aim to reduce its expenses **[1 mark]**
> - This means Ollie would have more money available to invest in equipment and resources needed to offer lessons for different musical instruments **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> Accept any other appropriate response

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure you do not simply state a financial objective — the command word "outline" means you need to identify the objective and then briefly develop it, ideally linking it to the context of the business. For example, do not just write "increase profit" — explain briefly why or how this relates to TADS. Also remember that the question says "other than revenue", so avoid mentioning revenue as your financial objective or you will not gain any marks.

**[2 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *Bella's Bistro* is a small café in a busy town centre. Bella, the owner, wants to introduce a wider range of homemade cakes and pastries. To achieve this, she will need to set clear business objectives.

Outline **one** possible non-financial objective that *Bella's Bistro* might have.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying a possible non-financial objective *Bella's Bistro* might have and 1 further mark for outlining it in the context of the business
> 
> "Outline" requires identification of a relevant point plus development or context
> 
> Any pair from (1 mark per point):
> 
> - Bella's Bistro could aim to improve customer satisfaction **[1 mark]**
> - By ensuring that customers receive friendly and efficient service so they are more likely to return and recommend the café to others **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - Bella's Bistro could aim to increase its market share in the local area **[1 mark]**
> - By attracting customers through its wider range of homemade cakes and pastries compared to competing cafés **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - Bella's Bistro could aim to improve employee satisfaction **[1 mark]**
> - So that staff are motivated to provide a better experience for customers visiting the café **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - Accept any other appropriate response
> 
> **[2 marks]**
> 
> 1 mark for identifying a valid non-financial objective and 1 mark for the correctly linked outline in the context of the business

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure you choose a genuinely non-financial objective — avoid objectives such as increasing profit or revenue, as these are financial objectives. Non-financial objectives relate to areas such as customer satisfaction, employee welfare, social responsibility or market share. Always link your answer back to the business in the extract to pick up the second mark. For example, refer to Bella's café, her cakes and pastries, or the town centre location rather than writing a generic answer.

**[2 marks]**

parts.problem_md: Explain **one** disadvantage for a business that does not achieve its predicted growth.
parts.solution_md:
The business may not generate enough revenue to cover its costs** [1 mark]**. This could lead to cash flow problems **[1 mark]**, making it difficult to pay suppliers or employees on time, which may threaten the survival of the business **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying a disadvantage for a business that does not achieve its predicted growth
> 
> 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the disadvantage, for a maximum of 3 marks
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Shareholders may not be very happy **[1 mark]** because if the business does not reach its predicted growth, they may not receive dividends **[1 mark]** and this may mean that they invest in other businesses **[1 mark]**
> - If the business does not achieve its predicted growth it may not be able to expand **[1 mark].** This means that it may lose some market share **[1 mark]** as customers could go elsewhere **[1 mark]**
> - Accept any other appropriate response.
> 
> Answers that list three disadvantages with no explanation will get 1 mark only
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md: Explain **one** disadvantage for a business that fails to meet its objective of maximising profit.
parts.solution_md:
The business may struggle to reinvest in new equipment or technology **[1 mark]**. This could mean it falls behind competitors who are able to innovate **[1 mark]**, leading to a loss of customers and reduced market share over time **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying a disadvantage for a business that fails to meet its objective of maximising profit
> 
> 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the disadvantage, for a maximum of 3 marks
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - The business may not be able to attract new investors **[1 mark]** because lower profits make the business less appealing **[1 mark]**, which could limit its ability to raise finance for future growth **[1 mark]**
> - Employees may become demotivated **[1 mark]** as the business may not be able to offer pay rises or bonuses **[1 mark]**, which could lead to higher staff turnover and increased recruitment costs **[1 mark]**
> - Accept any other appropriate response.
> 
> Answers that list three disadvantages with no explanation will get 1 mark only
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Tesco is one of the UK's largest supermarket chains, operating over 4,000 stores. In recent years, Tesco has faced increasing competition from discount retailers such as Aldi and Lidl, which offer lower prices. Tesco has set a non-financial objective to improve customer satisfaction ratings.

Analyse the benefits to Tesco of setting non-financial objectives such as improving customer satisfaction.
parts.solution_md:
By focusing on customer satisfaction, Tesco can build stronger customer loyalty **[1 mark]**. Satisfied customers are more likely to return to Tesco rather than switch to discount competitors like Aldi and Lidl **[1 mark]**, which helps Tesco maintain its market share despite the increasing competition it faces **[1 mark]**

Improving customer satisfaction can also help Tesco to differentiate itself from discount retailers **[1 mark]**. While Aldi and Lidl compete mainly on price, Tesco can stand out by offering a better overall shopping experience, such as higher quality service and product range **[1 mark]**. This could attract new customers and ultimately lead to increased revenue in the long term **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award up to 2 marks for identifying benefits to Tesco of setting non-financial objectives
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for applying the benefits to Tesco's context
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the benefits to the business
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Focusing on customer satisfaction can improve Tesco's brand reputation **[1 mark]**. If customers have a positive experience shopping at Tesco, they are more likely to recommend it to others through word of mouth **[1 mark]**, which could help Tesco attract new customers without spending heavily on advertising **[1 mark]**
> - Setting non-financial objectives like customer satisfaction can also motivate Tesco's employees **[1 mark]**. Staff who are encouraged to provide excellent service may feel more valued and engaged **[1 mark]** in their work, which can reduce staff turnover **[1 mark]**
> - Accept any other appropriate response
> 
> Answers that list three benefits to Tesco of setting non-financial objectives with no explanation will get a maximum of 1 mark
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md: Explain **one** benefit for a business of setting an objective to improve customer satisfaction.
parts.solution_md:
Customers are more likely to make repeat purchases **[1 mark]**. This can lead to a more stable and predictable revenue stream **[1 mark]**, reducing the need to spend heavily on attracting new customers **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Award 1 mark for identifying a benefit for a business of setting an objective to improve customer satisfaction 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the benefit, for a maximum of 3 marks
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - The business may gain a stronger reputation **[1 mark]** as satisfied customers recommend the business to others through word of mouth **[1 mark]**, which can increase the customer base without additional marketing costs **[1 mark]**
> - Employees may have a clearer focus on service quality **[1 mark]** because the objective gives them a specific target to work towards **[1 mark]**, which can improve overall business performance and competitiveness **[1 mark]**
> - Accept any other appropriate response.
> 
> Answers that list three benefits with no explanation will get 1 mark only
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> GreenLeaf is a small garden furniture business based in Wales. It started three years ago with just two employees and has grown steadily. The owner, Megan, initially set an objective to survive in the first year, but now wants to focus on increasing market share.

Analyse the reasons why GreenLeaf's business objectives may have changed over time.
parts.solution_md:
Now that GreenLeaf has been trading for three years and has grown steadily, survival is no longer a concern **[1 mark]**. This means Megan can shift her focus to more ambitious objectives like increasing market share **[1 mark]**, as the business is now in a stronger financial position to compete **[1 mark]**

As GreenLeaf has become more established in Wales **[1 mark]**, Megan may have identified opportunities to attract customers away from competitors by offering better products or prices **[1 mark]**. Focusing on market share now makes sense because growing the customer base will help secure the long-term future of the business and reduce the risk of being overtaken by larger rivals **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award up to 2 marks for identifying reasons why GreenLeaf's business objectives may have changed over time
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for applying the reasons to GreenLeaf's context
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the benefits to the business
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Megan's objectives may have changed because the business may have built up enough profit to invest in areas such as marketing or expanding its product range **[1 mark]**. This gives Megan the confidence to pursue growth **[1 mark]**, whereas in the early stages all of her focus and limited funds had to go towards simply keeping the business running **[1 mark]**
> - Accept any other appropriate response
> 
> Answers that list three reasons why GreenLeaf's business objectives may have changed over time with no explanation will get a maximum of 1 mark
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md: Explain **one** benefit for a business of setting an ethical objective.
parts.solution_md:
The business may attract more customers who value ethical practices **[1 mark]**. This can help to differentiate the business from competitors **[1 mark]**, leading to increased sales and market share **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying a benefit for a business of setting an ethical objective
> 
> 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the benefit, for a maximum of 3 marks
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - The business may find it easier to recruit and retain motivated employees **[1 mark]** because workers often prefer to be associated with a responsible employer **[1 mark]**, which can reduce recruitment costs and improve productivity **[1 mark]**
> - The business may build a stronger brand reputation **[1 mark]** as stakeholders such as customers and investors view the business more favourably **[1 mark]**, which can lead to greater long-term profitability and growth **[1 mark]**
> - Accept any other appropriate response.
> 
> Answers that list three benefits with no explanation will get 1 mark only
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> FreshBite is a food delivery business that operates in several cities across the UK. It has recently expanded into two new regions but has found that delivery costs are higher than expected. FreshBite's main financial objective is to increase profit.

Analyse how not achieving its financial objective of increasing profit might affect FreshBite.
parts.solution_md:
If FreshBite does not increase its profit, it may struggle to cover the higher than expected delivery costs in the two new regions **[1 mark]**. This could lead to cash flow problems, meaning FreshBite may not be able to pay its drivers or suppliers on time **[1 mark]**, which could disrupt the service and damage its reputation with customers **[1 mark]**

Not achieving its profit objective could also limit FreshBite's ability to grow further **[1 mark]**. Without sufficient profit, the business will have less money to reinvest into expanding into additional regions or improving its delivery operations **[1 mark]**. This could allow competitors to grow faster and take market share, leaving FreshBite in a weaker position across the UK **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award up to 2 marks for identifying impacts on FreshBite of not achieving its financial objective of increasing profit
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for applying the reasons to FreshBite's context
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the benefits to the business
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - If FreshBite fails to increase profit, it may be forced to cut costs in other areas **[1 mark]**, such as reducing the number of delivery drivers, which may lead to slower deliveries and dissatisfied customers **[1 mark]**. This could cause customers to switch to rival food delivery services **[1 mark]**
> - It could also make it harder for FreshBite to attract investment **[1 mark]** as investors want to see a business performing well financially before putting money in. If FreshBite cannot demonstrate growing profits, potential investors may look elsewhere **[1 mark]**, leaving FreshBite reliant on its own limited funds to deal with rising delivery costs in new regions **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> As We Grow (AWG) is a clothing business in Iceland. The social objective of the business is to use natural materials, such as wool, and produce environmentally friendly products. It aims to design clothes that will last a long time, to encourage families to buy fewer clothes and reduce waste in society.
> 
> AWG’s increasing product range now includes jumpers, dresses, shirts and baby clothes. These are produced in small workshops that employ family and friends. Waste is kept to a minimum and any leftover material is used to make scarves and hats. The business has one store in Iceland. It uses its website to advertise and sell its clothing online to customers in other countries. The business has received the Icelandic Design Award for its contribution to the environment.
> 
> AWG’s social objectives include the use of natural materials, being environmentally friendly and reducing waste.

Evaluate the impact on *AWG* of having these social objectives when planning to grow the business. You should use the information provided as well as your own knowledge of business.
parts.solution_md:
A social objective is a goal set by a business that aims to benefit society or the environment rather than focusing solely on profit **[K]**

Having social objectives can help AWG to grow by strengthening its brand image and reputation **[K]**. By using natural materials like wool and reducing waste, AWG has already won the Icelandic Design Award **[Ap]**, which gives the business credibility and positive publicity **[An]**. This can attract environmentally conscious customers both in Iceland and internationally through its website, leading to increased sales and supporting growth **[An]**

However, having these social objectives could make it more difficult and expensive for AWG to grow **[K]**. Using natural materials and keeping waste to a minimum may cost more than using cheaper synthetic alternatives **[K]**. As AWG expands its product range and tries to reach more customers in other countries **[Ap]**, these higher production costs could reduce profit margins **[An]**, making it harder to fund further growth. The small workshop model using family and friends **[Ap]** may also be difficult to scale up **[An]**

Overall, AWG's social objectives have a largely positive impact on its plans to grow **[E]**. In today's market, more consumers are looking for sustainable and environmentally friendly products **[K]**, so AWG's values give it a strong competitive advantage that can drive online sales worldwide **[An]**. While costs may be higher, these social objectives are central to what makes AWG unique and attractive to customers **[E]**. Without them, AWG would lose the identity that sets it apart from larger, cheaper clothing businesses **[Ap]** and would struggle to compete on price alone

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - **12-mark 'evaluate' questions are marked using a level-of-response grid (L1 - L3)**
> - Examiners judge how well the response demonstrates:
> 
>   - Accurate knowledge of relevant business concepts and terminology
>   - Application of ideas to the case study throughout the answer
>   - Logical chains of reasoning explaining business impacts linking points together to show clear cause and effect
>   - A clear, justified conclusion based on evaluation of the issues
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Social objectives may enable AWG to meet the needs and wants of customers → who care about the environment and are seeking a sustainable range of clothing
> - Minimising waste may enable AWG to reduce its costs → can pass on the cost savings to its customers to encourage more sales
> - It may be more costly to use natural material → may result in a high price for the jumpers and dresses → discourage some people from buying the clothes, resulting in slow growth for the business
> - Many people in society may not be concerned about social objectives and the environment → may be more concerned about current fashion → may lead to a decrease in sales revenue for *AWG*

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> SunnySide Bakery is a small bakery in the town of Whitby, England. It was set up five years ago by Maria, who wanted to sell freshly baked bread and cakes using traditional recipes. The bakery has built a loyal customer base and employs three full-time staff. However, a new supermarket has recently opened nearby, offering cheaper baked goods.

Maria is reviewing the bakery's objectives and is considering two options:

- Option 1: Set a financial objective to reduce costs in order to lower prices and compete with the supermarket.
- Option 2: Set a non-financial objective to improve product quality and customer service to differentiate SunnySide from the supermarket.

Justify which one of these two options SunnySide Bakery should choose.
parts.solution_md:
A business objective is a target or goal that a business sets out to achieve in order to guide its decisions and measure its success **[K]**

Reducing costs would allow Maria to lower her prices **[K]** and compete more directly with the new supermarket **[Ap]**. This could help SunnySide keep existing customers who might be tempted to switch to the supermarket for cheaper baked goods, protecting the bakery's revenue **[An]**

However, cutting costs could mean using cheaper ingredients or reducing staff hours **[K]**. This could lower the quality of SunnySide's traditional recipes and the level of customer service, which is what has built the bakery's loyal customer base over the past five years **[Ap]**. Maria could end up losing the very thing that makes her bakery special **[An]**

Improving product quality and customer service would help SunnySide stand out from the supermarket **[K]**. Customers who value freshly baked goods made with traditional recipes **[Ap]** are unlikely to find the same experience in a supermarket, so this objective could strengthen loyalty and attract new customers through word of mouth in Whitby **[An]**

The drawback is that improving quality and service may increase costs **[K]** for SunnySide. With only three staff and a small bakery **[Ap]**, Maria may struggle to fund improvements while the supermarket is already taking some of her customers, putting pressure on her income **[An]**

SunnySide should choose Option 2 **[E]**. A small bakery cannot realistically compete with a supermarket on price, so trying to cut costs would be a losing battle **[E]**. Instead, focusing on quality and service plays to SunnySide's strengths **[Ap]** and gives customers a clear reason to choose the bakery over the supermarket **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - **9-mark ‘justify’ questions are marked using a level-of-response grid (L1 - L3)**
> - Examiners judge how well the response demonstrates:
> 
>   - Accurate knowledge of relevant business concepts and terminology
>   - Application of ideas to the case study throughout the answer
>   - Logical chains of reasoning explaining business impacts
>   - A clear judgement, providing justification for the choice made
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Even if Maria does not lower her prices significantly, spending less on areas such as packaging or energy bills means more  revenue is kept as profit → giving the bakery a stronger financial position to deal with the increased competition from the supermarket
> - The supermarket can buy ingredients in bulk at much lower prices due to economies of scale → it will always be able to undercut Maria, no matter how much she reduces costs → making this objective potentially unrealistic.
> - Focusing on quality and customer service → could allow Maria to charge premium prices to customers in Whitby who appreciate handmade, traditional baked goods → increase SunnySide's revenue and profit despite cheaper supermarket alternatives
> - Improving quality and service takes time to show results → in the short term, SunnySide may continue to lose customers to the supermarket while Maria invests in improvements

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> CoastLine Surf School is a small business based in Jeffreys Bay, South Africa. It was set up three years ago by Jake, a former professional surfer, and offers group and private surfing lessons to tourists and locals. The business employs six part-time instructors during the busy summer months. Jake has noticed that some customers have complained about long waiting times for lessons, and that two of his instructors have recently left to work for a rival surf school.

Jake is reviewing the business's non-financial objectives and is considering two options:

- Option 1: Set an objective to improve customer satisfaction by reducing waiting times and offering a better booking system.
- Option 2: Set an objective to improve employee retention by offering better pay and training to instructors.

Justify which one of these two options CoastLine Surf School should choose.
parts.solution_md:
A non-financial objective is a business goal that is not directly related to making money, such as improving customer satisfaction or employee welfare **[K]**

Improving customer satisfaction by reducing waiting times would directly address the complaints **[Ap] **CoastLine has received.
